one_line_contribution: A component-decomposition of cross-backbone agent experience: at fixed retrieved items, fixed reader scaffold and matched tokens, deleting the writer's ReAct/think text (not converting the scaffold, and not paying for a model-aware rewriter) is claimed to recover most of the cross-backbone deficit, with authorship-swap arms (reader's own post-hoc thoughts over foreign actions, foreign thoughts over the reader's own actions) locating the harm in who wrote the reasoning rather than in the item as a whole.
closest_prior_work: Two verified threats, neither fatal. (1) arXiv:2605.30723 'Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All: Model-Aware Skill Alignment' (verified via s2cli, S2, 2026-05-29, 2 citations) is the named target: it establishes that skill utility is model-dependent and trains a lightweight rewriter to fix it. It does not decompose an item into thought vs action vs scaffold and does not run a delete-the-reasoning baseline, so it threatens P3's framing more than P1's claim — but the proposal only reimplements it as a *prompted* rewriter, so it does not actually contest 2605.30723's result. (2) arXiv:2509.23196 'From Harm to Help: Turning Reasoning In-Context Demos into Assets for Reasoning LMs' (verified, S2, 2025-09-27), which I found and the proposal did not cite, already documents the phenomenon-level claim that in-context demos carrying another model's reasoning *harm* reasoning LMs and proposes a test-time rewrite (Insight-to-Solve) as the fix. It is on QA/math, not agent experience memory; it does not manipulate writer identity, does not hold retrieved items fixed across serializations, and its baseline is direct answering rather than a stripped demo — so the proposal's cross-backbone estimand and its zero-cost-strip-vs-rewriter contest survive, but 'foreign reasoning text in the context hurts' is no longer a surprising claim, and a reviewer will read the title as overselling a known effect. Also relevant and uncited: arXiv:2403.14589 (ActRe/A3T, verified, S2, 19 citations) already generates post-hoc reasons for arbitrary action sequences, which is the F3/F5 teacher-forcing device applied to training data rather than in-context; and arXiv:2605.23899 (verified, S2, 15 citations) already reports that neither extractors nor consumers behave uniformly and that model-generated skills show non-trivial negative transfer.
strongest_objection: The headline interaction P1(c) is partly manufactured by headroom, not by producer-consumer mismatch. The same-backbone cells are the only control that excludes a pure token-efficiency/dead-weight account, and the proposal's own Step-0 numbers put a reader with a good pool at 0.807/0.869 success (Measurement A, expert->Q at k=3). A cell sitting at ~0.85 cannot show Delta_strip >= +5 on a percentage-point scale whatever the mechanism, so P1(b) (<= +1 same-backbone) is close to entailed by the ceiling and P1(c) = (a)-(b) inherits that. The design has no headroom correction anywhere: no odds/logit-scale or normalized-gain analysis, no matching of same- and cross-backbone cells on baseline success, no arm that puts a same-backbone cell at cross-cell success level. A reviewer will say the experiment cannot distinguish 'own thoughts are harmless because the reader wrote them' from 'own thoughts have no room to hurt because the cell is near ceiling', which is exactly the alternative P1 was built to exclude. Second, P3's null is nearly engineered: the rewriter is prompted rather than trained (the paper it is aimed at trains one), gets one regeneration and is then hard-truncated to the token count of an action-only strip, with validity checked only as mean tokens within 10% and never for well-formedness. 'A deterministic strip matches a model-aware rewriter' will not be granted from a truncated prompted proxy, and the title asserts it.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Pre-register a scale on which the writer x reader interaction is not ceiling-bound: report Delta_strip on the logit scale and as a fraction of remaining headroom alongside net points, and add one same-backbone cell whose baseline success is matched to the cross cells (e.g. a harder task subset or a degraded same-backbone pool), so P1(b) has room to fail. (2) Add the token-matched filler placebo described below; without it the F1r-F2 contrast is a length contrast with a plausible mechanism attached. (3) Either drop the rewriter claim to 'a prompted model-aware rewriter under a matched token budget adds nothing', or run the rewriter uncapped with tokens reported and score cost-adjusted, so the P3 result is about adaptation rather than about truncation; also report the fraction of F4 items that were truncated mid-item. (4) Fix the F6 selection: as the entailment check notes, choosing the two thoughts-only cells by largest verbatim deficit selects on an outcome-correlated criterion; add one same-backbone F6 cell and one smallest-deficit cross cell, pre-registered before Phase A is unblinded. (5) State the domain limit up front and, if budget allows after the pre-registered cut order, run one cross cell in a second domain (WebShop) — in ALFWorld the action sequence essentially is the procedure, which is the most likely reason the strip wins.
missing_baseline: A token-matched, content-neutral filler placebo: F1r with the writer's thoughts replaced by an equal number of task-irrelevant or generic text tokens in the same slot (the brief's own Appendix B demands token- and rate-matched placebos, and the wrong-type placebo blind1 is cited from Measurement C rather than re-run here). As written, F1r vs F2 differs in exactly the deleted thought tokens, and the only defense against a pure-length account is the same-backbone cells, which are ceiling-compressed. The filler arm separates 'the foreign author's reasoning specifically hurts' from 'any ~N tokens of non-action prose between the action lines hurt a foreign reader', and it is cheap: two cross cells at 4 seeds. A second, weaker omission: no arm that keeps the writer's thought *content* while normalizing its surface form (deterministic reformatting into the reader's thought template without regeneration), so 'authorship' in P4/P5 is confounded with style plus content plus post-hoc-ness rather than isolated.
preprint_collision: No verified collision, but the proposal's check is thinner than it presents, and I am scoring novelty on what I verified rather than on its assertions. Every query below ran through the literature command (s2cli.py, Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers, channels s2=ok hf=ok); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. My queries: (1) mechanism, unrestricted, 'removing chain-of-thought reasoning from in-context demonstrations improves performance action-only exemplars' -> CoT-prompting literature only (2409.04057, 2311.09277, 2410.21333), nothing on cross-model experience items; (2) mechanism, --recent, 'agent experience memory transfer across backbones reasoning traces written by another model hurt reader' -> 2607.28272 MemHarness, 2607.10608 The Compliance Trap, 2606.00642, 2512.16962 MemoryGraft — none decomposes an item into thought vs action; (3) --recent, 'which component of a stored trajectory transfers across models thoughts versus actions ablation memory item' -> memory-architecture papers only, empty on point; (4) closest named method, --recent, 'model-aware skill rewriter baseline deterministic stripping no adaptation matched tokens cross-model skill reuse' -> 2605.30723, 2608.06880, 2606.01139, 2606.01311, plus 2608.11079 and 2608.05604 (two distinct SkillZip papers) — all adapt or compress whole skills, none runs a zero-cost strip as the baseline; (5) 'reasoning style mismatch between demonstration author and consumer model in-context learning negative transfer rationale' -> 2509.23196, 2509.22230, 2504.01738 'Style over Substance', 2601.03717 MIND; (6) --recent, 'in-context demonstrations containing chain-of-thought harm reasoning models remove rationales from demos' -> safety-benchmark noise, empty on point; (7) 'ALFWorld retrieved trajectory exemplars action observation only versus ReAct thought annotated cross model agent success' -> 2403.14589 ActRe, 2505.00234, 2607.13884. Verified IDs the proposal relies on: 2605.30723, 2608.06880, 2606.01311, 2606.01139, 2605.11032, 2603.13260, 2512.20908, 2509.23574, 2306.14050, 2604.15877, 2606.00642, 2604.01161 — all resolve and match their descriptions. Two IDs it lists as evidence do NOT support the claim made for them: 2608.24232 is TRACE, a safety benchmark for reasoning traces, and 2608.10232 is FACT, failure-aware causal training for world-action models in robotics; neither is about in-context demonstrations from another model, so query (1) of the proposal's own check effectively returned nothing on topic and is reported as coverage. 2608.13760 could NOT be verified — not found on S2 or HF. The check also missed the two nearest items I found (2509.23196, 2403.14589) and its home-literature query stopped at parametric distillation, which is where the in-context analog was most likely to have been scooped. Net: novelty is real but narrower than the title, and the collision check earns a deduction rather than a neutral.
